reader.requirement: At --std 85, USAGE BINARY is radix 2, with alignment and representation (sign included) as the implementor documents (DOC-A.1-205: big-endian two's complement, 1/2/4/8 bytes, no alignment). It must allocate storage for the full range of the decimal PICTURE, which at 85 is up to 18 digits including P positions, scaled or not, signed or not.

edition-consulted.switches: numeric item digit limit: 18 at COBOL-85, 31 at 2002+ (COBOL0802 for 19-31 at 85)
edition.Extension flags vendor spellings (COMP-1..COMP-5) only under the extension-flagging option; BINARY/COMP/COMPUTATIONAL/PACKED-DECIMAL/DISPLAY map to one Usage at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|Edition.|CobolVersion in Model/PicInfo.cs, Model/DataItem.cs and Runtime CobolNum.Image.cs: none. The only edition read is the 18-digit cap, which makes the 16-byte tier unreachable at 85.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no within the 1985 range (gr3a identical at 2023); yes in range: 19-31 digit BINARY pictures are refused at 85 (COBOL0802) and take the 16-byte tier at 2002+
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf12_05 covers S9(4)/S9(9)/S9(18) extremes and the S9(4) image; it does not cover the 1-byte and 8-byte tiers' images, unsigned 1-digit, scaled V and P items, ODO with a BINARY object, or the 19-digit refusal

probes.expected: Each width holds its PICTURE's extreme. Images are big-endian two's complement as documented. ADD past the PICTURE maximum is a size error. An ODO object of USAGE BINARY works.

probes.printed: error COBOL0802: ... 19 digit positions; COBOL-85 limits fixed-point items and literals to 18 digits
probes.expected: 1985 caps a numeric item at 18 digit positions, P counted (the 1985 PICTURE 'P' rule), so a 19-digit BINARY picture is refused

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.5.14.4 GR3  (5.14.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3

reader.notes: The width ladder is sufficient for every 1985 picture: SPP99 BINARY is one byte, enough for its unscaled maximum 99. Probe values at each tier round-trip, and the group byte images match DOC-A.1-205. A 0xFF image byte is the HIGH-VALUE character, whose ORD is 65536 by the documented native-alphabet design. This is not a BINARY defect.

refuter.evidence: Read PicInfo.StorageWidth (Binary: <=2 digits 1 byte, <=4 2, <=9 4, <=18 8, else 16) and PicInfo.Truncation (Binary -> DigitCount, no edition read). Signed 1-byte holds -99..99, 2-byte -9999..9999, 4-byte 10^9-1, 8-byte 10^18-1: every 1985 picture (18-digit cap, COBOL0802 at 85) fits, P positions not stored. BINARY arithmetic in r2b (DIVIDE REMAINDER, ROUNDED, CORRESPONDING, UNSTRING counters) correct. Reader's gr3a covered images and ODO. cite.py: OK  §1985:VI.5.14.4 GR3  (5.14.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3.
